input.summary: Limit Vendor audits to once per 12 months on 30 days' notice, during business hours, by an independent auditor, and remove remote system access.
input.comment: [Playbook] We can accommodate usage verification, but our playbook requires audits to be no more than once every twelve months on 30 days' written notice, during business hours, by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, and without access to our systems. We have also removed the remote-access right, which conflicts with Section 22.2's existing no-direct-access protection.

ops.oldText: Vendor may audit Customer at any time without notice and may remotely access Customer's systems and records for that purpose.
ops.newText: Vendor may audit Customer's use of the Services no more than once in any twelve-month period, on at least thirty days' prior written notice, during Customer's normal business hours and without unreasonably disrupting Customer's operations. Each audit shall be conducted by an independent auditor bound by written confidentiality obligations, and Vendor and its auditor shall have no remote or direct access to Customer's systems; Customer will instead provide relevant usage records.
